articles.title: Warning Issued Over Trespassing at Abandoned Asbestos Factory in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Landowners of the derelict Turner Brothers factory have warned against trespassing, citing dangers from asbestos and potential fires.
articles.content_html:
Landowners of the abandoned asbestos factory in Rochdale have issued a warning to trespassers who enter the site. The decaying Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area has become a hotspot for urban explorers, despite the dangers associated with the hazardous materials present.

Spodden Park Ltd, the site owners, anticipate an increase in trespassing during the summer holidays and have expressed concerns about the risk of fires due to the dry weather. They have stated that breaking into the site is a crime and that they will contact the police if their security measures are breached.

The site remains dangerous, with asbestos fibres posing a health risk to anyone who enters. Experts have noted that these fibres can lead to serious health issues, including mesothelioma and lung cancer. The owners have urged parents to educate their children about the risks associated with the site, including the potential for injury and the legal consequences of trespassing.

Spodden Park Ltd has repaired the perimeter security fence and continues to take measures to secure the site. They have requested that anyone witnessing trespassing report it to the police. Plans for redevelopment of the former factory are in consideration, but the site currently remains in a state of decline.

articles.title: Shisha Lounge Closed After Carbon Monoxide Exposure
articles.excerpt: Phantom The Lounge in Rochdale has been ordered to close after environmental health officers discovered excessive carbon monoxide levels, putting customers and staff at risk.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 31 July 2026 at 10:28. 3 source updates have been combined into this article.

A shisha lounge on Maclure Road, Rochdale, has been handed a closure order after excessive levels of carbon monoxide (CO) were found on site. The order was granted at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on 24 July 2026, following evidence presented by environmental health officers from Rochdale Borough Council, with support from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service and Greater Manchester Police.

Phantom The Lounge was found to be operating illegally, with smoking taking place in a substantially enclosed area, violating the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006. Inspections revealed hazardous practices in the kitchen, including the use of an electric fan to smoulder hot coals in an unventilated area, leading to CO levels exceeding 100 parts per million (PPM) in the kitchen alone.

On two occasions, fire service officers insisted that customers and staff leave the premises for their safety. Despite the council offering the owners an opportunity to rectify the issues, the business did not cooperate and continued operations without making necessary changes, prompting the council to take legal action.

Councillor Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader and portfolio holder for Climate Change and Environment, stated that the high levels of CO posed a significant risk to health. She commended the environmental health officers and partners for their intervention, which prevented further danger to the public.

articles.title: Phil Eckersley Promises Support for Greater Manchester Boroughs Ahead of Mayoral Election
articles.excerpt: Conservative mayoral candidate Phil Eckersley has pledged to enhance support for Greater Manchester's boroughs, addressing crime and housing issues in an interview.
articles.content_html:
Phil Eckersley, the Conservative candidate for Mayor of Greater Manchester, has pledged to provide more support to the boroughs of the region in an interview with the source. He expressed concern that too much focus has been placed on the city centre, leaving towns on the outskirts, including Rochdale, feeling neglected.

Eckersley highlighted the rise in crime in the boroughs, stating that residents are 'too scared to walk home after 8pm' due to fears of anti-social behaviour. He attributed part of this issue to the Greater Manchester Police, claiming they have not effectively addressed these concerns. He called for increased stop and searches and a greater police presence across the region, rather than just in the city centre.

In addition to crime, Eckersley aims to build more affordable homes throughout Greater Manchester, focusing on developing brownfield sites to protect green spaces. He also promised to support local businesses, asserting that he would be the 'most pro-business mayor Greater Manchester has ever had.'

Eckersley's policies align closely with those of Labour candidate Bev Craig, particularly regarding affordable housing and support for boroughs outside the city centre. However, he believes Labour has failed to deliver for the region during their time in control of the mayoralty since 2015. The Greater Manchester Mayoral by-election is scheduled for Thursday, 30th July.
